newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian pension fund law set for launch on Aug 11.
newsitem.headline: Italian pension fund law set for launch on Aug 11.

text.p: An Italian government decree establishing regulations for private pension funds will take effect on August 11, the Labour Ministry said on Thursday.
From then, companies wishing to set up new funds for individual investors, firms or entire industrial sectors will be able to apply for authorisation from the ministry, the statement said.
Italians have traditionally relied almost exclusively on the generous state pension system, but the government has been looking for some time to shift some of the burden onto the private sector.
Some pension funds have already been set up ahead of the formal introduction of the decree, with around 3.2 million people expected to start investing from the outset.

The Italian insurance association (ANIA) said in a recent report that it expected some 45 trillion lire ($24 billion) would be sunk into the funds initially, with this figure rising to 80 trillion lire by the year 2000 and 150 trillion by 2020.
Italy originally signalled its intention to liberalise the pension fund market in 1995 but the government took months to work out regulations for the sector.

Some research bodies believe the funds will draw less cash than expected because the government is allowing only limited tax deductions on money invested in the various programmes. ($ = 1845 Italian Lire)
